html:
The Moche flourished on the north coast of Peru from about 100 to about 750 CE, in desert river valleys around modern Trujillo.

They were probably not one empire. Most scholars now see several Moche polities, northern and southern, sharing one culture and religion. The southern centre near the town of Moche held two giant adobe platforms, the Huaca del Sol and the Huaca de la Luna. The Huaca del Sol was built from millions of mud bricks, many stamped with marks that may name the groups who made them.

The Moche are known for:

  • Pottery: lifelike portrait vessels of individual faces, and scenes of daily life, war, sex, healing and ritual sacrifice.
  • Metalwork: gold, silver and copper ornaments. The royal tombs found at Sipán in 1987 showed how rich a lord could be.
  • Irrigation: canals that turned desert valleys into farmland.

Their art shows a ceremony in which captives taken in ritual combat were sacrificed and their blood offered to a lord. Burials at Sipán matched these scenes.

The Moche declined in the 500s to 700s, a time of severe El Niño floods followed by drought. Their lands later passed to the Chimú, who saw themselves as heirs of the coast. They were contemporaries of the Nazca to the south, and later felt the pull of the highland Wari.
sum: The Moche flourished on the north coast of Peru from about 100 to about 750 CE, in desert river valleys around modern Trujillo.
